newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone rations gasoline.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone rations gasoline.

text.p: Sierra Leone ordered fuel rationing for motor vehicles on Tuesday, saying the West African nation was short of gasoline and diesel.
"Petrol stations should sell only three gallons (11.4 litres) to private cars and five gallons (19 litres) to taxis and passenger vans daily," state radio reported, quoting a government order.
Trade officials say a tanker bringing fresh supplies by sea was expected to arrive from Ivory Coast before the end of the week.
Throughout the nation the price of fuel and fares for transport have doubled.
Drivers and their vehicles have formed long queues at service stations in the capital Freetown over the past two days. Children and workers have had to walk to and from school and work.
Trade industry officials, meanwhile, said the International Monetary Fund was pressing the government to drop fuel subsidies, which were contributing to a $5 million budget deficit.
Finance Minister Thaimu Bangura told parliament in a 1997 budget speech before Christmas that the government planned to halt gasoline subsidies by March.
